prompt: Challenge C138-CH1: Our die-cutting machine is producing burrs and uneven creases on micro-corrugated E-flute when humidity in the hall goes above 65% — box com

content.text: {"expertise":[{"text":"Research focuses on thermomechanical processing of starch-based materials and establishment of correlations between processing parameters and mechanical properties of resulting films, using in-line rheological monitoring.","sources":[{"id":"R1044","field":"bio","quote":"establishing correlations between screw configuration, processing temperature, and tensile or barrier properties"}]},{"text":"Work demonstrates how moisture content during extrusion affects material properties, with specific attention to processing conditions and their quantification through direct measurement techniques.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-07550","field":"abstract","quote":"five consecutive extrusion cycles under identical processing conditions (145 °C, 150 rpm, 24 wt% moisture)"}]},{"text":"Research provides practical guidance on moisture management and in-line monitoring strategies relevant to packaging production at scale, including methods for relating processing parameters to material performance.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-10760","field":"abstract","quote":"Practical guidelines are provided for screw design selection, barrel temperature profiling, and moisture management"}]}],"fit":"partial","fitReason":"The researcher's expertise in processing parameters, rheological monitoring, and property correlations [R1044, SYN-PUB-10760] is adjacent to the challenge's core issue, which is environmental humidity affecting pre-existing corrugated board rather than formulation or extrusion control of new material; the work addresses material processing and moisture but not ambient moisture effects on finished product performance or humidity sensing systems."}
